question: Which grouping forecasts a measured sacrum path and future bilateral leg surface voltage during visual rotation?
source: Peterson & Ferris, OpenNeuro ds003739 v1.0.3, f15449b6aecb83044b49a1798955e8a212a68fc1; same qualified 18 development, six historical comparison people. Six reserve people excluded. Historical retrospective comparison; no fresh cohort.
source_reader: Use only originally qualified, fully paired events from both visual rotation postures. Require at least one usable central scalp channel. Past window c-159..c where c=ceil(rotation onset at 256 Hz)+32. Future c+1..c+32. Same registered person, task/unique native session, event ordinal, direction, original event third and cutoff for every input and outcome. Source offline filtering and conditional quality are limitations of prospective interpretation.

signals.scalp: D19/A1/B22, nominal C3/Cz/C4, author-good and finite, reject an exact constant run >=32 samples in the history. Five consecutive 32-sample bins of signed mean and log1p(RMS / 1 microvolt). Scale observed measurements on training people and carry availability flags. Scalp electrodes mix biological sources.
signals.leg: Eight leg EMG channels, four per leg: tibialis anterior, soleus, medial gastrocnemius, peroneus longus. Same five bins of log1p(RMS / 1 microvolt). Indicates muscle electrical activity (excitation). No direct recordings of peripheral nerve, contraction length/shortening, muscle force or torque.
signals.position: Measured three-axis sacrum displacement in stored mm relative to c, last sample of twenty nonoverlapping 8-sample past bins. The anchor has zero relative displacement.
signals.physics: Four deterministic, event-specific inertial projections, each giving a 3D end-displacement in mm at 125 ms. v_tau=(p[c]-p[c-lag])/(lag/256 s), delta_p_sim=v_tau*0.125 s for lags 8,16,32,64. Assumes constant velocity, zero net acceleration across the forecast horizon. Assumption only; draws on the same measured positions. All input endpoints are representable in the position stream. No independent fourth sensor, forces, gravity inversion or contact estimates.

target: Eight measured future leg RMS voltages in microvolts, and the three-dimensional optical marker displacements at 32 later samples in mm. Fit four 3D knots at samples 8,16,24,32 and linearly interpolate from the observed zero anchor. Fit muscle targets in log1p(RMS / 1 microvolt) and decode to nonnegative microvolts. All model variants have the same targets.

architectures.paired: Each stream gets its own learned 16-wide tanh projection. A branch takes two projections and their componentwise product, learns a 16-wide tanh representation. Pair scalp with leg and measured displacement with projected displacement. Fuse the two learned branches, their componentwise product and two common context fields (posture and direction) into a learned 32-wide tanh layer, then predict both targets with a common linear head.
architectures.early: After the four learned per-stream projections, apply the normalized order-four Hadamard transform along stream identity before either branch. Every resulting vector contains all four inputs. Use exactly the same two learned bilinear feature blocks, final fusion and head. Early orthogonal mixing is one explicit comparator, not every possible early-fusion network.
architectures.crossed: Identical model with scalp paired with measured position, and leg excitation paired with projected displacement.
architectures.controls: Separately fit six copies of the paired architecture with the standardized values for one of scalp, muscle, position, physics, scalp+muscle, or position+physics zeroed throughout fit and evaluation. Scalp presence flags retained in every copy. Also use untrained persistence (previous 32-sample RMS and a stationary sacrum) and previous 32-sample secant velocity with the same muscle persistence. Wrong-event tests use the frozen full paired model and jointly borrow scalp+EMG or position+physics, or scalp alone, from the latest strictly earlier nonoverlapping event of the same person, posture/session, cue, event-log third and identical scalp availability. Donor cutoff plus 71 must precede recipient cutoff minus 198. Borrowed position and derived physics always travel together. Mismatch can break cross-group consistency. Use the exact same donor-eligible rows for each matched baseline.

fit.draw: Sampling with replacement. Each person gets equal total probability, each of the four posture-by-direction cells gets equal share within each person. Uniform rows within each cell. Identical indices and initialization per seed across models.
fit.optimizer: AdamW lr 0.002, weight decay 0.01, float32, no dropout, no hyperparameter search. Equal weight to mean smooth L1 loss (beta=1) on each standardized target group, eight EMG channels and twelve path knots.
fit.scales: Development-only means and population standard deviations per field, including separate learned-target scales. Scalp moments from present sites only. Standardization floor 1e-6 replaced by 1. No per-person adaptation.

score: Within each event, endpoint (i) mean absolute eight-channel RMS error in microvolts, (ii) mean Euclidean 3D distance across all 32 timepoints in millimetres. Average errors across seeds, not predictions. Equal weight to direction then posture then whole people. Report phase and whole cohort, plus final-sample distance. Six historical people held out as whole units across both postures. 10,000 participant-paired bootstrap draws, seed 431, two-sided descriptive 95% intervals. No independent inference from events or seeds.
decision: Report ranks on both endpoints separately. Claim the requested grouping outperforms the two named alternatives only if all FOUR predeclared paired-minus-alternative contrasts (two outcomes times two alternatives) have mean < 0 and one-sided Bonferroni 98.75th percentile < 0. Comparisons to baselines and information controls are descriptive; a second independent population is needed for a topology claim.
timing: Benchmark a fixed 32-update prefix and 128 example prediction on development inputs at CPU threads 1, 2, and available GPU with default kernels. Keep CPU1 unless a candidate is faster end-to-end and absolute per-output difference <0.01 standardized units. Report full fit time and warmed batch and one-event forward time. No real-time or remote-device claim.
